text: {"executive_summary": "RCS-APP-02, a high-tier retail application PD scorecard, receives an overall amber rating. Discrimination and calibration are both green: test AUC is [[performance.test_auc]] with limited overfitting (AUC drop [[performance.auc_drop]]), and mean predicted default of [[calibration.mean_predicted]] aligns with the observed rate of [[calibration.observed_rate]]. The amber rating is driven by two areas: a synthetic out-of-time tranche showing score drift above the green threshold, and fairness evidence where the age-group equalized odds difference is amber and the foreign worker group is too small to test. The rebuild reproduces the Gate 3 model's test predictions exactly, so the conclusions apply to the approved implementation. All results rest on a single 300-row test sample and a synthetic time ordering, which limits the strength of the assurance.", "sections": {"performance": "Test AUC is [[performance.test_auc]] (Gini [[performance.test_gini]], KS [[performance.test_ks]]) on [[performance.test_n]] test records with a [[performance.test_event_rate]] event rate, rated green. The bootstrap confidence interval runs from [[performance.test_auc_ci_low]] to [[performance.test_auc_ci_high]], so the lower bound sits close to the green threshold and the point estimate should be read with that uncertainty in mind. The gap between train AUC of [[performance.train_auc]] and test AUC is [[performance.auc_drop]], indicating no material overfitting.", "calibration": "Calibration in the large is strong: mean predicted default of [[calibration.mean_predicted]] against an observed rate of [[calibration.observed_rate]], a relative deviation of [[calibration.calib_ratio_dev]]. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test gives a p-value of [[calibration.hl_pvalue]] (statistic [[calibration.hl_statistic]]), so there is no evidence of misfit across risk groups. The Brier score is [[calibration.brier_score]]. Both calibration checks are green, supporting use of the PDs as estimates rather than rank orderings only.", "stability": "Train-to-test score PSI of [[stability.score_psi]] and a largest characteristic CSI of [[stability.max_csi]] (age) are both green, showing no meaningful population shift between samples. The synthetic out-of-time back-test is amber: the worst tranche score PSI is [[stability.tranche_max_psi]], above the green limit, although the weakest tranche AUC of [[stability.tranche_min_auc]] suggests ranking power holds up. Because the tranches are ordered by record id rather than by true application date, this result is indicative only and cannot confirm behaviour through time.", "fairness": "Approval rates under the [[fairness.score_cutoff]] cut-off (overall approval [[fairness.test_approval_rate]]) show adverse impact ratios of [[fairness.sex_adverse_impact_ratio]] for sex and [[fairness.age_group_adverse_impact_ratio]] for age group, both green. The sex equalized odds difference of [[fairness.sex_equalized_odds_difference]] is also green. The age-group equalized odds difference of [[fairness.age_group_equalized_odds_difference]] is amber, meaning approval rates among good or bad applicants differ more across age groups than the green limit allows. Age is a model input, which makes this difference worth understanding. The foreign worker comparison could not be rated because one group has only 9 records."}, "findings": [{"severity": "medium", "section": "stability", "finding": "The worst synthetic out-of-time tranche shows a score PSI of [[stability.tranche_max_psi]], above the green threshold, while train-to-test PSI is green. The tranches are an id-ordered split rather than true time periods, so the drift signal cannot be attributed to genuine temporal change.", "recommendation": "Run a true out-of-time back-test on dated application data before or shortly after deployment, and set up periodic score PSI and CSI monitoring with escalation triggers in the ongoing monitoring plan."}, {"severity": "medium", "section": "fairness", "finding": "The age-group equalized odds difference is [[fairness.age_group_equalized_odds_difference]], above the green limit, and age is a direct model input. The foreign worker comparison could not be rated because one group has only 9 records.", "recommendation": "Model Development should investigate which age bands drive the gap, assess whether the age bins are justified by risk evidence, and test alternatives such as coarser banding or constraints. Fairness testing for foreign worker status should be repeated on a larger sample or with pooled data, and the age result should be tracked in ongoing monitoring."}], "limitations": ["Validation uses German Credit (UCI) with a single fixed 700/300 split, so the test sample of [[performance.test_n]] records gives wide uncertainty on discrimination metrics.", "No application date exists, so the out-of-time back-test is a synthetic ordering by record id and does not demonstrate performance or stability through time.", "The foreign worker group (A202) is too small to assess, so fairness for that attribute remains untested.", "Fairness testing uses a single decision rule (cut-off [[fairness.score_cutoff]]) and a single favourable outcome definition; other cut-offs and intersectional groups were not assessed.", "The data is a public benchmark rather than the bank's own portfolio, so representativeness of the bank's applicant population, economic conditions and reject-inference effects were not assessed."]}
